C1.rationale: Level 1 anchor: collaboration/teamwork appears in the graduate attributes and in the generic-skills lists of the compulsory core subjects, but no compulsory core unit documents an assessment of collaborative practice. Level 2 requires a core unit to assess collaborative practice (group project with individual accountability, client/stakeholder work, interprofessional activity). The only assessed stakeholder work in the program is the capstone needs assessment (MEDS90033), which the handbook places under the 'Coursework option', not under the 'Core Subjects' heading, and which Research-pathway students never take; per the downward-resolution rule this pathway-conditional subject does not lift the item to 2. The MEDS90006 hurdle requires posting to a discussion board and sharing philosophies with other students, which is peer interaction rather than assessed collaborative practice with individual accountability. Level 3 additionally requires an assessment coordinating work across people AND tools/AI systems; no gen-AI, tool-allocation or human-plus-system division-of-work evidence appears anywhere in the extract.

C2.rationale: Level 2 anchor is met in compulsory core assessment: MEDS90007's reflection essay (35%) requires appraisal of the quality of the student's own implemented teaching plan against an evidence-based rationale; MEDS90009's hurdle requires critique of an existing curriculum against the subject's theoretical materials; MEDS90011's essay requires critique of a research method against 'best practice'. This is criterion-referenced appraisal of quality, not merely reflection claimed in outcomes (which would be level 1). Level 3 is not taken: no assessment requires students to document and justify reliance decisions on a tool, source or collaborator, and there is no AI-output-quality evidence anywhere in the extract. The MEDS90007 plan-then-reflect pair is the closest candidate for the 'evidence strategy adjustment over time (process-focused assessment)' route, but the adjustment is documented once retrospectively in a single essay rather than tracked across iterations, so the ambiguity between 2 and 3 is resolved downward.

C4.rationale: Level 3 anchor: 'The program documents structured progression toward independent learning: a self-scoped capstone or research project'. Every student completes exactly such a project in the final year regardless of pathway — either the Minor Thesis, where the student develops and investigates their own research question and defines research questions based on their own practice, or the capstone, where the student designs a new curriculum for their own practice. Both are self-scoped by design and both are assessed by weighted, substantial written artefacts (thesis report; written presentation of curriculum), satisfying R2's requirement of assessment evidence rather than an outcome statement. Progression is documented structurally by the prerequisite chain requiring at least 75 points of coursework including Research Methods before the thesis may commence, and by the capstone's stated function of integrating learning from the earlier Graduate Certificate and Diploma content. This exceeds level 2 (a single core assessment applying methods to a novel problem) because the independence is program-structural, not task-local.

C5.rationale: Level 2 anchor: students design and conduct an inquiry with methodology selection and data collection, assessed. The Minor Thesis documents exactly this — designing and implementing a research project, seeking human research ethics approval where appropriate, designing methodologies, analysing and reporting results, assessed by a thesis draft report and a thesis report. Level 3 is explicitly blocked by its own qualifying clause, 'a substantial project generating primary evidence is REQUIRED (not one route among several)': the handbook states the degree is completed via either the Research or the Coursework pathway, and Coursework-pathway students complete a curriculum-design capstone rather than a primary-evidence project. The universally compulsory methods subject stops short of level 2 on its own — its major assessment is a research proposal (methodology selection and a Gantt chart, but no data collection), and its hurdle is explicitly a simulated exercise rather than real data collection. Level 2 is therefore carried by the thesis route only, and level 3's 'required' test fails.

W2.rationale: Level 3 requires both clauses and the handbook documents both from compulsory core evidence, scored on documented task features only (R4), not on any 'real world' label. Spine, not a single instance: MEDS90007 assesses a session teaching plan aligned with the student's current practice (40%); MEDS90009 explicitly escalates the same artefact from the micro session plan of Subject 2 to the program/curriculum level (50%); MEDS90011 assesses a research proposal with literature critique, theoretical framing, method selection and a scheduled Gantt chart (80%); and the final year is a capstone curriculum or minor thesis that the capstone description states integrates the earlier course content. That is at least one practitioner artefact per stage plus a capstone with earlier scaffolding. Genuine constraint of practice: the MEDS90007 plan is designed, delivered and reflected on in workplace-based activity, so the recipients are real surgical trainees and the task requires a measure of outcome for those recipients — a consequential audience and the profession's own standard of performance; the capstone additionally supplies an externally scoped problem (a stakeholder needs assessment establishing conditions and scope) and real resource limits (faculty requirements, settings, equipment and other resources). Level 2 is exceeded because the artefacts are not one instance, and the tasks are not merely scenario-framed academic work (level 1) — they produce the artefacts a surgical educator produces, judged against instructional-design criteria.

W3.rationale: Scored on the v4.2 in-practice route. The cohort is documented as already practising: the course is 'designed to support surgeons in developing expertise in teaching' with online delivery for busy professionals undertaking studies in conjunction with clinical commitments, and core assessment is anchored in 'their current practice'. Core unit MEDS90007 meets the in-practice level-2 anchor: participants 'will be required to design, deliver and reflect on their own teaching' in workplace-based activities; the assessed teaching session must be aligned with their current practice and include a 'measure of outcome for students who are recipients of the teaching' — real recipients plus a documented outcome measure — and the implemented delivery is assessed via the 35% reflection essay on the teaching plan they implemented, satisfying R2's assessment-evidence requirement. Level 3 is not reached: it requires a required SEQUENCE of assessed own-practice activity with structured reflection and documented accountability to workplace stakeholders. Only MEDS90007 requires conducted own-practice activity of every student — MEDS90009's alignment with actual practice is merely 'encouraged' and is curriculum design (an artefact, homed in W2), and MEDS90033's stakeholder needs assessment exists only on the Coursework pathway, so it is not required of the cohort. Accountability to workplace stakeholders is gestured at by the recipient outcome measure but never documented as an assessed criterion. The own-practice activity therefore stands alone, and ambiguity resolves downward to 2. One-construct-one-home is respected: the MEDS90007→MEDS90009→MEDS90011 artefact spine stays homed in W2; W3 counts only the work-situated participation element. No placement, practicum or supervised external workplace component appears anywhere in the structure, so the placement route alone would not support level 2.
evidenceLines: The program is designed to support surgeons in developing expertise in teaching and to promote educational scholarship. There are core and elective subjects. The program content reflects critical issues in the broader education community together with specific challenges for surgical education – the role of regulatory bodies, balancing clinical service with training, teaching and learning in the workplace, ethical imperatives for simulation-based education, and safer working conditions including safe hours. Students complete a capstone or minor thesis in their final year. The online delivery mode offers flexibility essential for busy professionals undertaking studies in conjunction with clinical commitments.

ambiguities: C1 (1 vs 2): the capstone MEDS90033 assesses genuine stakeholder work (a needs assessment of stakeholders, 'Written report on needs assessment', 20%), which would satisfy the level-2 anchor's 'client or stakeholder work' clause. It is not scored as level 2 because the handbook lists only four subjects under the heading 'Core Subjects' and places the capstone under the 'Coursework option', so Research-pathway students never take it. Resolved downward per the never-resolve-upward rule. If the pathway-required capstone were treated as core, C1 would be 2.

C1 (1 vs 2, second route): the MEDS90006 hurdle requires contributing to a discussion board and sharing educational philosophies with other students, which is assessed peer interaction but not a group project with individual accountability, client work, or interprofessional activity. Treated as insufficient for level 2.

C2 (2 vs 3): MEDS90007 assesses a teaching plan (40%) and then a reflection on that plan as implemented (35%), requiring students to state why elements need development and how they will make those improvements. This is arguably the level-3 route 'evidence strategy adjustment over time (process-focused assessment)'. Resolved downward because the adjustment is documented once, retrospectively, in a single essay rather than tracked across iterations, and because no reliance-decision or AI-output-appraisal element exists anywhere in the extract.

W1 (1 vs 2) and the W1/W2 boundary: the session teaching plan, the program/curriculum design essay and the capstone curriculum document are plausibly 'recognised professional genres' for a surgical educator, which would satisfy W1 level 2. Per 'one construct, one home' they are scored in W2, whose construct names the form of the result and the fidelity of the task; W1 keeps audience and professional conduct, and no core assessment documents an audience beyond the tutorial group and teaching team. Note also that the handbook labels these design tasks 'Essay', an academic genre wrapper, which reinforces the downward resolution.

W2 (2 vs 3): the strongest constraint-of-practice evidence (stakeholder-scoped conditions; faculty, settings, equipment and resource specification) sits in the pathway-conditional capstone. Level 3 is nevertheless taken because the clause is independently satisfied from compulsory core evidence — the MEDS90007 plan is delivered in workplace-based activity to real trainees and must include a measure of outcome for those recipients, and MEDS90011 requires a scheduled research proposal. The spine clause is also met from core alone (MEDS90007 to MEDS90009 to MEDS90011, plus a final-year capstone or thesis).

W3 cohort-practising status: the 'Entry and participation requirements' page is not captured in the extract (navigation heading only). Practising status was established from the course overview ('designed to support surgeons', 'busy professionals undertaking studies in conjunction with clinical commitments') and assessment text ('aligned with their current practice', 'their own teaching'). Accepted as documented cohort evidence; had it been rejected, ambiguity-down on the placement route alone would have yielded 1.

W3 double-home risk: the MEDS90007 teaching-plan and reflection essays belong to the assessment spine homed in W2. Resolved by one-construct-one-home: W3 scores only the own-practice participation they evidence (required workplace delivery to real recipients with an outcome measure, and the assessed reflection on the implemented session); the authentic-artefact fidelity of plan/curriculum/proposal remains W2 and was not re-counted.

W3 (2 vs 3): 'Students are encouraged to design curriculum aligned with their actual practice' is encouraged, not required, and is artefact design; MEDS90033's stakeholder needs assessment is required only on the Coursework pathway. No required sequence of assessed own-practice activity exists for the whole cohort, and the recipient outcome measure approaches but does not document accountability to workplace stakeholders as an assessed criterion — resolved downward to 2.

[superseded by v4.2 re-score 2026-08-16; retained for the audit trail] W3 (0 vs 1 vs 2): none of the three anchors fits cleanly. Level 0 is excluded because workplace-based activity is documented in a compulsory core subject; level 2 is excluded because no placement, practitioner supervision or host accountability appears anywhere; level 1's exemplars (elective, optional, unassessed) fit imperfectly because the activity is core and feeds assessment. Scored 1 as the lower of the two live readings. The underlying mismatch is cohort-structural: the anchors assume a pre-professional cohort placed into a host workplace, whereas this cohort are practising surgeons learning within their own existing practice, which the program does not supervise.

Elective availability: MEDS90015 Simulation in Surgical Education, MEDS90016 Teaching Surgical Science, MEDS90017 Educational Leadership in Surgery and MEDS90018 Assessment and Evaluation in Surgery are all marked 'Not available in 2026'. Their assessments (including the MEDS90016 hurdle 'design and deliver a teaching session' and the MEDS90017 formal debate) were therefore not used as scoring evidence for the 2026 offering, and in any case are elective, not core.
notScoreable: The AI-specific clauses of C1 level 3 ('coordinating work across people AND tools/AI systems') and C3 levels 2-3 (core units addressing AI capabilities and limitations/ethics; critique or governance of AI systems) could not be tested: the extract contains no occurrence of artificial intelligence, gen AI, machine learning or any equivalent in any course page, subject overview, learning outcome, generic-skills list or assessment description. Both items were still scoreable on their non-AI evidence (collaboration for C1, digital/e-learning for C3), so neither is left unscored — but the absence, not a judgement about AI content, is what caps them.
